title: Vessel and oak
what: Where the Lot ages and how loudly the wood speaks: steel, an old 1 000 L Fuder, neutral, first-fill or new barriques (French or American), and the toast.

steps: American oak holds far more oak lactone
so it smells of coconut as well as vanilla

choose: Steel or an old Fuder keeps Riesling's fruit in front: a Fuder has far less wood surface per litre. New barriques give vanilla, toast and oak tannin; each reuse gives less. Heavier toast shifts the oak towards smoke and toast.
exam: Expect 'describe the effects of new oak' or 'why use old casks?'. Separate flavour, tannin and slow oxygen, and say which matters for the style.

check.question: Your Côte d'Or Chardonnay from first-fill French barriques shows only faint oak. You want clearly more vanilla and toast, but no coconut. What do you change?
check.why: Each reuse leaves a barrel with fewer oak compounds, so a new barrel gives far more vanilla and toast than a first-fill one. French oak is subtler and spicier; American adds sweet vanilla and coconut; an old Fuder gives little oak.
